enumeration.method: Independent font-sensitive enumeration of all 25 main pages finds exactly CMBX10 Theorem headings 1,4,5,6. Lemma 2, Remark 3 and Proposition 7 share the numbering sequence but are excluded from the Theorem inventory. Theorem 5 continues from page 15 onto page 16. Figure 8 ends the main text on page 25; the saved heading crop establishes Appendix A on a separate page 26.

checks: Inventory and final census pass separate validator invocations. The independently reviewed inventory hash is unchanged, and every original theorem field survives the handoff.
The title, three authors, arXiv v2 stamp of 21 September 2023, separate title-page date of 22 September 2023, versioned URL, 41-page count and PDF hash match the inspected source.

All four theorem bodies were visually checked on pages 8,10,15,16,17. Theorem 5 retains its full page continuation, all three assumptions, both distributional limits, the additional condition (25), mean convergence and both variance limits.

Eleven interfaces preserve original model, lfdr, monotonicity, maximum criterion, support-line procedure, weighted loss, oracle, null estimate, modified rule, regret and Chernoff definitions. Their natural-language keywords and selectors are source-backed.

Theorem 1 retains its exact last-rejection identity without monotonicity; the shape condition appears only in the final max-lfdr clause. The source empty-rejection convention and reordered labels are resolved.

The constrained rule in Theorem 4 uses the specific plus-one null-proportion estimate and weak cutoff p_(k)<=lambda. Its connection to ordinary SL is conditional on the unconstrained threshold lying below lambda.

Theorems 5 and 6 do not acquire the particular estimator (12), the constrained rule (13), or the proof-only Grenander implementation. Theorem 6 quantifies an arbitrary estimator under its original one-sided error condition.

The negative m exponent in Theorem 5(25), the one-sided condition in Theorem 6(iii), and the exact regret coefficient are preserved rather than repaired. Source-domain omissions and the reversed abstract description of lfdr are recorded separately.

Seven auxiliary passages resolve sorted labels, cost-derived alpha, population threshold, fixed-threshold regret and constrained-versus-unconstrained distinctions. Nine source notes retain limitations without altering original statements.

The final graph has 22 direct uses and 25 deduplicated same-paper connections. Independent scope assertions confirm estimator-specific and regret-specific reach, and all mathematical evidence lies on main pages with balanced TeX grouping braces.

source_notes: This is a census of the pinned arXiv v2 preprint; equivalence to journal wording has not been established.
The original asymptotic tail assumptions and any resulting mathematical issues remain source claims. This audit preserves statements and dependencies without certifying the proofs.
Appendix bodies were excluded. All objects needed to state the inventoried theorems are available in the main text.

unresolved_source_references.note: The abstract describes lfdr as the probability that a null hypothesis is false. Equation (2) explicitly defines it as P(H_i=0 | p_i=t), meaning the null is true. The actual definition is preserved; the abstract wording is not used to reverse the event.

The density-ratio formula is a version of a conditional probability given a continuously distributed p-value. Pointwise values at zero-density points are not specified; the endpoint pi_0=0 can produce 0/0 away from the support. The max-lfdr definition assigns zero to an empty set, and the empty-rejection term in (11) must likewise be read as zero without evaluating an undefined H_(0).

Non-increasing f_1 gives the required non-decreasing lfdr in the nondegenerate mixture setting. The converse need not identify the shape of f_1 when pi_0 is 0 or 1. The source equivalence is preserved, and Theorems 5/6 explicitly restrict pi_0 to (0,1).

The last-minimizer rule and p_(0)=0 are explicit. Theorem 1 prints ell<=1 without an explicit lower bound; Theorem 4 does not print an ell range. Ell is used as a nonnegative testing level in context. The constrained rule uses p_(k)<=lambda despite the prose below lambda. The k>=0 range implicitly ends at m because only m order statistics exist. No change is made to either original statement.

Equation (7) uses a maximum and a weak lfdr inequality under monotonicity, without a global continuity or endpoint-version condition that always guarantees attainment. Theorems 5/6 add unique interior crossings and local smoothness, avoiding an ambiguous threshold in their own setting. The empty-set convention remains tau*=0.

Assumption (iii) uses m^(1/3)(ell-hat-ell) converging to zero in probability. The additional condition (25) instead prints m^(-1/3)|ell-hat-ell| inside a tail probability. That weaker-looking exponent is preserved exactly; no expected positive exponent is substituted for it.

The source requires only P{m^(1/3)(pi-hat_0-pi_0)>epsilon}=o(m^(-2/3)), without an absolute value or a lower-tail condition. This alone does not imply two-sided consistency, despite the preceding specialization discussion. A two-sided condition is not silently imported from Theorem 5.

The explicit estimator (12) is strictly positive but may exceed one, and no clipping is specified. Theorem 6 allows any estimator under its printed one-sided condition, without separately requiring pi-hat_0>0; alpha/pi-hat_0 therefore needs a convention if it is zero. Theorem 5 likewise does not specify a domain for the random ell-hat. These omissions are recorded instead of supplying an unstated truncation.

The proofs of Theorems 4 and 5 and the asymptotic analysis are deferred to Appendix A. Only its heading crop was inspected. All objects required to state the saved Theorems are resolved from the main text; no appendix proof assumptions are imported.

ambient_resolution.shared: D1 fixes an iid two-groups experiment of size m: H_i=0 is a true null, H_i=1 a non-null, conditional p-values have densities f_h on [0,1], and the null is uniform. The marginal f and cdf F are in D1. All expectations and probabilities average both H and p under this model, unless the text explicitly conditions. H denotes the whole binary vector. D5 defines sorted p-values, p_(0)=0, the last-minimizer convention, the rejection count R_ell, set R_ell in calligraphic type and threshold tau_ell. A2 defines H_(k). Standard ambient objects include indicator functions, finite maxima, order statistics, conditional probability versions, expectation, variance, Bernoulli laws, differentiability, probability/distribution limits and deterministic little-o. In the asymptotic sections the mixture parameters and densities are fixed as m grows. A1 fixes omega>0 and alpha=1/(1+omega); ell is a tuning level and lambda a cutoff, while epsilon is an arbitrary positive tail tolerance.
ambient_resolution.1: D1 resolves model (1), the uniform null and pi_0 in [0,1]. D5 resolves procedure (4), R_ell and its last-rejection threshold, with ell<=1 as printed and the nonnegative-level interpretation from context. A2 resolves the reordered label H_(R_ell); the guard R_ell>0 prevents a nonexistent rejection from contributing. D2 defines lfdr. The first exact identity does not require D3. Only the final sentence additionally requires non-increasing f_1, so D4 max-lfdr equals the last-rejection quantity. No BH procedure, null-proportion estimator, Chernoff distribution or loss function is required.
ambient_resolution.4: D1 and D3 give the two-groups model, uniform null and non-increasing alternative. Lambda is fixed in (0,1). D8 is pi-hat_0^lambda from (12), including the plus one and the strict count p_i>lambda. The theorem binds the constrained index and rejection set inline; D9 retains those definitions and D5 supplies the order-statistic and last-minimizer conventions. D4 is the expected maximum lfdr with zero for no rejection. A5 records the conditional relation to the ordinary estimated-level rule, without replacing the constrained procedure. The estimator asymptotics on page 11 are not assumptions of this finite-sample result.
ambient_resolution.5: D1,D3 fix the iid uniform-null mixture with pi_0 strictly between zero and one and a non-increasing alternative. Ell is fixed in (0,1/pi_0). The theorem itself binds the unique interior t_ell satisfying f(t_ell)=1/ell, requires C1 regularity near t_ell and f-prime(t_ell)<0, and quantifies any random ell-hat with m^(1/3)(ell-hat-ell) tending to zero in probability. A3 connects t_ell to the population optimizer; D5 defines the data threshold tau_(ell-hat), and D2 its lfdr. D11 defines Z as the maximizer location of unit two-sided Brownian motion minus t squared. The two distributional limits are followed by the additional tail condition (25), then mean convergence and both variance limits. The printed negative exponent in (25) is retained. No particular null-proportion estimator or Grenander implementation is imposed.
ambient_resolution.6: D1,D3 fix the iid mixture with pi_0 in (0,1), uniform null and non-increasing alternative. A1 fixes the cost-derived alpha. D2 and D7 resolve lfdr and the oracle tau*, which this theorem additionally binds as a unique interior crossing lfdr(tau*)=alpha, with C1 density near tau* and negative derivative. The estimator pi-hat_0 is arbitrary subject to the original one-sided condition (iii); it is not necessarily D8 and is not silently assumed to satisfy a two-sided bound. D5 defines ordinary SL at alpha/pi-hat_0. D10 defines the unconditional empirical Bayes regret through weighted loss D6 and oracle D7, not the population fixed-threshold proxy in A4. D11 supplies the same Chernoff variable Z and its variance. The conclusion is deterministic convergence of the scaled expected regret with the exact printed -1/3 coefficient. A6 preserves the preceding specialization explanation without adding hypotheses to the theorem.
